subject: Vendr inventory claiming playbook & scoped SOC2 evidence plan
messages:

Subject: Vendr inventory claiming playbook & scoped SOC2 evidence plan

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the quick intake on Vendr. To make the Whistic/Vendr profile handoff as low-friction as possible, we put together a short "inventory claiming" playbook that fits the SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ evidence model and the Vendr upload flow. Attached: vendr_inventory_template.csv (claim mapping + example values) and presign-instructions.pdf (S3 presign manifest and TTL guidance).

High level ask: can Brightleaf confirm (by reply) who on your side will be the owner for each of the claim buckets in column "ClaimOwner" on the CSV (networking, host config, app controls, data controls, logging)? We propose the following split unless you want to alter it: Brightleaf -> networking & infrastructure; Brightleaf -> host config; Redwood -> data controls & key rotation; joint -> logging/access evidence.

Timeline proposal:
- Today: Brightleaf confirms owners + send portal_access_matrix if you want us to map fields into Vendr profile (you can attach or grant us a short-lived upload).
- By 3/27: Redwood provides presign manifest and sample manifest hash for your S3 staging bucket.
- 3/28: 30-min handoff call to walk the playbook and run one sample upload.

A few implementation notes up front:
- Presigned uploads: we recommend 24-hour TTL for manifest links to avoid stale uploads. Presign details in presign-instructions.pdf.
- Evidence types we expect: PDFs (policies), CSV/TSV (config inventories), TLS cert chains (text), filtered logs (redacted), and KMS rotation proof (screenshot or KMS ARN + rotation schedule).
- Redaction: PII should be redacted before upload. If you need, we can provide an example redaction checklist.

If that all looks good, reply with owner confirmations and any constraints (S3 vs direct Vendr upload, SSO/SCIM access, or NDA).

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

— Rishi

Rishi —

Thanks, this looks sensible and the attachments are helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we lock owners and the call time: 

1) Access/logging evidence: for SOC2 we can provide filtered CloudTrail and application access logs. Do you accept gzipped JSONL for log slices or do you prefer CSV? We typically provide compressed JSONL but can transform to CSV if that makes mapping easier.

2) KMS proof: we can share the KMS key ARN and a short rotation audit (screenshot or export). Is the ARN + rotation schedule enough for the Vendr claim, or do you prefer a signed attestation from our infra team?

3) Redaction guidance: can you share the redaction checklist you mentioned? We have a couple of PII-heavy records and want to make sure uploads meet your expectations.

We attach our portal_access_matrix.xlsx — it maps our internal fields to the common CAIQ/SIG questions. If you (or Jonas) can map those into the CSV template and drop a partially filled example back, that would speed the upload.

We can do the 30-min call; 3/28 at 10:00am PT works for our security lead.

Thanks —

Thanks Alice — quick answers inline and a small mapping note.

On Thu, 23 Mar 2028 at 09:45 Alice Chen <alice.chen@brightleaf.com> wrote:
> 1) Access/logging evidence: for SOC2 we can provide filtered CloudTrail and application access logs. Do you accept gzipped JSONL for log slices or do you prefer CSV?

We accept gzipped JSONL. The Vendr manifest supports content_type: application/gzip and we ingest JSONL slices. For the CSV template we included a "LogSampleType" column so you can indicate whether the evidence file is JSONL.gz or CSV. No need to transform unless you prefer.

> 2) KMS proof: we can share the KMS key ARN and a short rotation audit (screenshot or export). Is the ARN + rotation schedule enough for the Vendr claim, or do you prefer a signed attestation from our infra team?

ARN + rotation schedule is sufficient for initial ingestion. For the SOC2 claim we'll map that to the "KMS key management" control and flag it as "owner-provided artifact". If you have a signed attestation (pdf) that speeds later audit refreshes but is not strictly required for the first-pass profile.

> 3) Redaction guidance: can you share the redaction checklist you mentioned?

Attached in-line here: short checklist (you can paste into your workflow):
- Remove full SSNs and emails in log entries (replace with <redacted> and preserve timestamp + event_id)
- Hash user identifiers with SHA256 if traceability is required but PII must be hidden
- Remove authorization tokens and full JWTs, keep token_id only
- Keep timestamps, event_id, resource_id, and action fields

Operational notes:
- Presign TTL: 24 hours for manifests; individual artifacts may use longer TTL but prefer 72 hours max to limit accidental exposure.
- Manifest format: single JSON manifest with entries: filename, md5/sha256, content_type, claim_field, owner, upload_timestamp. We included an example in presign-instructions.pdf.
- Ownership mapping suggestion (fill the CSV like this):
  - networking: Brightleaf
  - host_config: Brightleaf
  - data_controls: Redwood
  - key_management: Brightleaf (provide KMS ARN)
  - logging: joint (Brightleaf uploads logs, Redwood pins log retention policy claim)

Next steps I will:
- Drop a partially populated vendr_inventory_template.csv into the shared drive by EOD (example values filled from your portal_access_matrix).
- Share the presign manifest sample (sha256 hash of sample manifest) so you can validate uploads.

If that sounds good Rishi, I'll prepare the sample and we can run the upload on the 3/28 call you suggested.

— Jonas

- Redaction: use the checklist Jonas provided; if you hit edge cases, mark files with "review-needed" in the manifest so we triage with you during the call.
